description: Analyzes Midnight’s Children through the politics of the children’s conference, Partition and war, kinship and gender, Rushdie’s multilingual English, and state control of bodies during the Emergency. Distinguishes historical events from the novel’s fictional participants and Saleem’s explanations; considers the limits of making one person stand for a nation; offers close-reading exercises; and traces publication, prizes and reception.
